extracted.intended_audience: students (pre-service and in-service) enrolled in MAT 240 / middle grades mathematics teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus and course/chapter description for MAT 240: Geometry for Middle Grades Teachers, including course objectives, assessment scheme, policies, instructional model (ACT), and modeling heuristic (DECAL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Grading Scheme (points and letter cutoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your grade will be based on the following: 5 Assignments 20 points each = 100 points; 5 Quizzes 20 points each = 100 points; 1 Project = 50 points; 2 Exams 100 points each = 200 points; 1 Final Exam = 100 points. There are 550 points possible. Your grade will be determined by the total number of points you earn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grade cutoffs: 495–550 points = A; 440–494 = B; 385–439 = C; 330–384 = D; 329 points or below = F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class Attendance and Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance will be taken. If you cannot attend a class meeting, it is your responsibility to notify the instructor and make arrangements to discuss the outcomes of the class discussion and assignments. You are expected to check Blackboard regularly for announcements, class notes, exercises, and assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation and presence are tied to credit and staying on pace; instructor expects students to use Blackboard and be responsible for missed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments Submission and Late Work Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive credit for assignments, they must be complete and submitted on the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in extreme circumstances, subject to the approval of the instructor, will late work be accepted or make-up exams given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Tools and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracing paper and dot paper (both with square and triangular designs), straightedge, compass, protractor, The Geometer’s Sketchpad software (highly recommended), calculator, and access to the Internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometer’s Sketchpad software is available in labs; students are encouraged to purchase the student version (~$40). Dot paper is posted on Blackboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exams and Quizzes Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Quizzes will precede Exams by about one week and will give you an idea of what to expect on the Exams. There will be two Exams in addition to the Final Exam. Exams after the first will be cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content for Exams will come from in-class notes, class notes on Blackboard, exercises on Blackboard, computer activities, class discussions, and assignments. Quizzes are posted online using WebCT and have deadlines (e.g., must be completed by the following Friday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Honor Code Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The work you do in this course is subject to the Student Honor Code. The Honor Code is a commitment to the highest degree of ethical integrity in academic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are bound by the Student Honor Code neither to give nor receive any unauthorized aid on examinations, quizzes, or any graded assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students with Disabilities Accommodation Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Students with disabilities who require accommodations (academic adjustments, auxiliary aids or services) for this course must register with the Disability Services Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Disability Services Office in the University Center, Suite 320 or call (859)572-6373 for verification and to receive reasonable academic accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites and Enrollment Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Prerequisites: MAT 141 with a grade of C or better. MAT 240 is open only to students majoring in elementary or middle grades education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have any doubt about your readiness for this course, you should discuss this with the instructor as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 1: Classify and describe plane figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to classify and describe plane figures including polygons and polyominoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 2: Determine, describe, and classify tessellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine, describe, and classify tessellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 3: Determine and describe plane congruence
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine and describe the congruence of two geometric objects in a plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 4: Determine and justify similarity of plane figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine, describe, and justify similarity of plane figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 5: Describe plane isometries and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to describe isometries in the plane and determine the image of a figure under an isometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 6: Determine symmetry of plane figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine the symmetry of plane figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 7: Classify and describe space figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to classify and describe space figures, including polyhedra and polycubes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 8: Determine and describe congruence in space
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine and describe the congruence of two geometric figures in space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 9: Describe isometries in space and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to describe isometries in space and determine the image of a figure in space under an isometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 10: Determine symmetry of space figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine the symmetry of space figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 11: Determine and justify similar figures in space
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine and justify similar figures in space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 12: Relate areas/perimeters of similar plane figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine and justify the relation of areas (and perimeters) of similar figures in a plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 13: Relate volumes/surface areas of similar space figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to determine and justify the relation of volumes (and surface areas) of similar figures in space.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Outcome 1: Problem solving in geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to solve problems in geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Outcome 2: Use of dynamic software
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to use dynamic software to aid in problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific software referenced includes Geometer’s Sketchpad and custom Java applets/graphing utilities; applets are available for download and may be incorporated into other courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Outcome 3: Use mathematical modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should use mathematical modeling to solve geometric problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling schema (DECAL) and techniques like finite differences and least squares are taught as modeling tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Outcome 4: Make conjectures from observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should make conjectures based on their observations of geometric phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course emphasizes conjecture generation and justification as part of mathematical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Outcome 5: Present clear and concise explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to present clear and concise explanations of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written, oral, and visual modes of communication are essential; presentations of findings to classmates are part of the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Outcome 6: Reason mathematically
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to reason mathematically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging in inquiry activities, employing reasoning skills, and linking concrete and abstract concepts are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACT paradigm: Active Assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Active Assignment: reading assignment (text or research article), Focus questions, and Focus problems; a quiz based on the reading is posted online and must be completed by the following Friday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active Assignment is posted by Friday for a Monday class; the discussion board is available from posting time as an asynchronous component to prepare for class.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACT paradigm: Conceptual Class
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual Class session discusses topics from the reading, relates mathematics to middle school classroom situations, and gives insights into Focus questions that students discuss on the discussion board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptual Class is recorded so it is optionally synchronous; students are encouraged to participate while it is recorded but can access the recording later.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACT paradigm: Talk Together (synchronous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk Together is a less formal online office-hours format where ideas from the discussion board are explored and students can request elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talk Together class is a mandatory synchronous session to provide a sense of community and pace; experience shows in-service teachers need mandatory scheduled activities to remain on pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: DECAL modeling heuristic
rubrics_metrics.description: DECAL: Describe the problem (identify known relationships/laws); Explore (employ critical thinking, inductive/deductive reasoning, visualization); Create a model relevant to the information and setting; Apply the model to answer the question; Link the model to new situations to check validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finite differences are useful when data follow a simple mathematical law (combinatorial or low-noise physics data); least squares is applied to minimize error in constrained models and discussed with NCTM applet illustrating why outliers affect error strongly. Finite differences less useful for noisy social science data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of vignettes to surface misconceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Vignettes (short classroom scenes) are used to bring points into focus from research readings and to spark discussion in online forums and class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vignettes focus on common student misunderstandings (examples given: confusion about even/odd, misconceptions about primes, confusion between rational and irrational numbers) and are used to elicit teacher discussion about addressing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of multiple representations and inquiry-based learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewing problem solving with multiple approaches and multiple representations can facilitate making connections among areas of mathematics and between mathematics and real-world problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students will work individually and cooperatively, use manipulatives, computers, and calculators when appropriate, and engage in inquiry activities to employ reasoning and link concrete and abstract concepts.
